lead.headline: Union Pacific trains killed 156 trespassers a year in 2023-25, nearly double 2015-17's 79; other railroads, same counties: up 30%
lead.number: UP-reported train-strike trespasser deaths: 79 a year (2015-17) → 156 (2023-25); UP's full count, including non-train deaths on its property, 97 → 200; other railroads in the same counties rose about 30%
lead.watch_out: A third of UP's recent reports use a stand-in age of 40 (4% in 2015-17), so part of the jump may be a change in how UP files; there's no suicide field

Per-train-mile rates of train incidents have remained comparatively low, and rates of injuries or fatalities have held steady; grade crossing incident rates have risen and erased earlier safety gains. Trespassing deaths, in particular, have nearly doubled on a per-train-mile basis since 2015 after over a decade of stability (see Figure 1 ). The number of railroad hazmat spills has remained low, both in comparison with railroad performance in past years and with other modes; no hazmat-by-rail spill has resulted in a fatality in over a decade. In November 2024, a pedestrian was also fatally struck by a Union Pacific freight train on Florin Road in South Sacramento, an incident that caused major traffic delays while Union Pacific and local authorities investigated.
